demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Memory.value: I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it
When I remember the frightening event I feel like it is happening right now.
The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me

vignette: Ahmad, a 78-year-old Middle Eastern man and an environmental scientist, has been experiencing significant distress following a traumatic incident at work where he accidentally caused serious injury to a colleague. The event occurred during a routine field study in the mountains. Ahmad was guiding his team through a treacherous trail when he stepped on loose rocks that dislodged a boulder. His colleague, who was walking behind him, was struck by the falling rock and suffered severe injuries. Since then, Ahmad has been struggling with the memory of this event, which continues to haunt him. When he tries to recount what happened, he often finds himself unable to articulate his feelings or describe the sequence of events clearly. He feels like there are words that should be there but somehow slip away when he tries to speak about it. The trauma has profoundly affected Ahmad's daily life and work environment. One particularly potent trigger for him is hearing heavy breathing sounds, which remind him of the frantic moments after the accident as he tried to help his injured colleague before emergency services arrived. This sensitivity has led Ahmad to avoid going out in nature or engaging in physical activities that might expose him to such sounds. Feeling happy or relaxed also serves as a trigger for Ahmad; these positive emotions often bring back vivid and overwhelming memories of the event, making it seem like he is reliving it right then and there. This has made social gatherings at work difficult. He finds himself avoiding interactions with colleagues during lunch breaks or team-building activities where such feelings might arise. Ahmad's wife has noticed that his behavior has changed significantly over time. They have been married for many years, but now Ahmad avoids physical affection like hugs, believing that any expression of closeness might trigger another wave of distressing memories and sensations. This avoidance has led to a noticeable strain in their relationship, as she feels he is withdrawing from her. Over the past several months, Ahmad's avoidance behaviors have escalated. He tries to avoid situations where he thinks he might encounter triggers, which has impacted his work performance significantly. His job often requires him to be out in nature or work closely with colleagues, both of which are now fraught with anxiety and fear. Despite his best efforts to focus on his professional responsibilities, Ahmad finds himself distracted by the constant threat of reliving the traumatic event. The culmination of these challenges led Ahmad to seek help finally. He is most afraid that he will never be able to return to work or have meaningful interactions with those around him without being consumed by fear and guilt. At the same time, he is hopeful that therapy might provide him with tools to manage his symptoms and reconnect with both his colleagues and his wife. In therapy sessions, Ahmad has expressed a deep sense of responsibility for what happened but also recognizes that it was an accident. He had come to believe that if only he could have been more careful or alert, the injury would never have occurred. His thoughts are filled with self-blame and concern about how his actions impacted his colleague's life. The therapist works closely with Ahmad to understand these beliefs and helps him reframe them in a way that acknowledges human fallibility without diminishing his sense of empathy for those affected by the incident. Through this process, Ahmad begins to see ways he might engage more fully with life again, even as he continues to grapple with the memory of what happened. Overall, Ahmad's journey reflects a complex interplay between traumatic memories and daily life experiences that have led him to seek help at this critical juncture.
